[[File:Raul Gonzalez 10mar2007 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Raúl González|Raúl]] is Real Madrid's all-time appearance record holder.]]
[[File:Cristiano Ronaldo, 2012 2.JPG|thumb|upright|[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] is Real Madrid's all-time record goalscorer.]]
[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]] is a professional [[association football]] club based in [[Madrid]], Spain, that plays in [[La Liga]]. The club was formed in 1902 as Madrid Football Club and played its first competitive match on [[1902 Copa de la Coronación|13 May 1902]] when it entered the final of the [[Copa del Rey|Campeonato de Copa de S.M. Alfonso XIII]].<ref name="Real Madrid turns 106 (I)">{{cite web | title = Pre-history and first official title (1900-1910) | url = http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202730681095/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_turns_106_(I).htm | publisher = [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] | access-date = 12 July 2008 | author = Luís Miguel González | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20081229094130/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202730681095/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_turns_106_%28I%29.htm | archive-date = 29 December 2008 }}</ref> Real Madrid was one of the founding members of La Liga in [[1929 La Liga|1929]], and is one of three clubs, along with [[FC Barcelona]] and [[Athletic Bilbao]], to have never been relegated from the league.<ref name="Real Madrid turns 106 (III)">{{cite web | title = A spectacular leap towards the future (1921-1930) | url = http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202730681768/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_turns_106_(III).htm | publisher = [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] | date = 28 February 2007 | access-date = 12 July 2008 | author = Luís Miguel González | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20081229093213/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202730681768/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_turns_106_(III).htm | archive-date = 29 December 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title = Classic club – Athletic Bilbao | url = https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/clubs/club=31071/index.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090717095550/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/clubs/club=31071/index.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = July 17, 2009 | publisher = [[Fédération Internationale de Football Association]] |access-date =13 September 2009}}</ref> Since then, the club's first team has competed in numerous nationally and internationally organized competitions. Real is [[List of football clubs in Spain by major honours won|the most successful club]] in [[Football records and statistics in Spain|Spanish football]], having won 71 domestic titles; a record 36 La Liga titles, 20 [[Copa del Rey|Spanish Cups]], 13 [[Supercopa de España|Spanish Super Cups]], 1 [[Copa Eva Duarte]], and 1 [[Copa de la Liga|League Cup]]. Real is the most successful club in [[List of UEFA club competition winners|European]] and international football, having won 35 official UEFA and FIFA trophies in total.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.archive.uefa.com/footballeurope/club=50051/domestic.html|title=Football Europe: Real Madrid CF|publisher=[[UEFA|Union des Associations Européennes de Football]] (UEFA)|access-date=2010-07-25|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100603055708/http://en.archive.uefa.com/footballeurope/club=50051/domestic.html|archive-date=2010-06-03}}</ref>

[[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] holds the record for most overall appearances, having played 741 from 1994 to 2010, ahead of [[Iker Casillas]], who made 725 appearances from 1999 to 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/clubs/club=366/index.html |title=Classic club: Real Madrid |publisher=[[Fédération Internationale de Football Association]] |access-date=11 September 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130305121834/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/clubs/club%3D366/index.html |archive-date=5 March 2013 }}</ref> [[Manuel Sanchís Hontiyuelo|Manuel Sanchís, Jr]] is third with 710 appearances from 1983 to 2001 for the club. [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] is the all-time top scorer with 450 goals in 438 appearances from 2009 to 2018. He holds the record for the most goals in a season for Real Madrid, Ronaldo scored 61 in all competitions during the [[2014–15 Real Madrid CF season|2014–15 season]] and also holds the record for second most league goals scored in a season in La Liga, with 48 goals in [[2014–15 La Liga]]. [[Karim Benzema]] is the second-highest scorer with 354 goals, having overtaken Raúl, who is third with 323 goals, in August 2022.

Real Madrid has employed numerous famous players, with four [[FIFA World Player of the Year]], twelve [[Ballon d'Or]]/[[FIFA Ballon d'Or]], four [[European Golden Shoe]] and three [[FIFA Club World Cup]] [[List of FIFA Club World Cup awards#Golden Ball|Golden Ball]] winners among the previous and current club players.

As of 22 August 2026, a total of 806 players have played at least one official match for Real Madrid throughout history. [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] is the player with the most appearances, with 741 matches, while more than 100 players have played only one match. In terms of minutes played, [[Iker Casillas]] has the most with 64,920 minutes, while the player with the fewest minutes is [[Pedro Mosquera]], who played just one minute. Alongside Spain, players from 46 different nationalities have played for Real Madrid. Argentinians are the most represented with 34 players throughout history, followed by Brazilians with 28 players, and then the French with 22 players.

==Key==
===General===
<div style="max-width: 800px; font-size:85%;">
* Appearances, goals and assists are for first-team official games, including those in [[La Liga]], [[Copa del Rey]], [[Copa de la Liga]], [[Copa de la Coronación]], [[Copa de la Coronación#Consolation Trophy / Copa de la Gran Peña|Copa de la Gran Peña]], [[Supercopa de España]], [[Copa Eva Duarte]], [[UEFA Champions League]], [[UEFA Europa League]], [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]], [[Latin Cup]], [[UEFA Super Cup]], [[FIFA Club World Cup]], [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]], [[FIFA Intercontinental Cup]] and [[Copa Iberoamericana]].
* The following list '''does not''' include [[List of association football competitions#Pre-season friendly / invitational tournaments|pre-season friendly / invitational tournaments]], nor does it include regional tournaments such as [[Campeonato Regional Centro]] and [[Copa Federación Centro]]. This list also '''does not''' include the [[1927–28 Spanish Football League|La Liga Minimalista]] competition which was held between 1927 and 1928.
* Substitute appearances are included.
* A player '''must''' have participated in at least <u>one official match</u> to be included in the list. The list does not include players who transferred to Real Madrid without playing any matches, those who were called up but did not appear on the field, or those who played in friendly matches without participating in official ones.
* The years refer to the '''[[Season (sports)|sport season]]''' in which the players played their first and last matches with the team, <u>not</u> the calendar years.
* Players are listed according to the total number of games played. If two or more players are tied, their rankings are determined as follows:
{{ordered list|start=1
 | Seniority, the date of the player's first match with the team.
 | goals scored
}}
</div>

===Table headers===
* '''Player''' – Nationality, first name and last name or nickname.
* '''Position''' – Role on the field of play.
* '''Real Madrid career''' – Playing career at the club.
* '''Captaincy''' – Captaincy period at the club.
* '''Matches''' – Number of games played.
* '''Goals''' – Number of goals scored.
* '''Assists''' – Number of assists provided, the following numbers is based on the assists criteria according to Opta, where assists are not counted for balls that are deflected or rebounded off opposing players and have clearly affected the trajectory of the ball and its arrival to the recipient (the goal scorer). Assists are also not counted for penalty kicks, direct goals from corners or free kicks, or own goals.
* '''Notes''' – Notes of the player's information.

==Notes==
; Awards and positions
*<small>d'Or</small>. {{note label|ballon||a}}{{note label|ballon||b}}{{note label|ballon||c}}{{note label|ballon||d}}{{note label|ballon||e}}{{note label|ballon||f}}{{note label|ballon||g}}{{note label|ballon||h}} Won the [[Ballon d'Or]] while at Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|author=Moore, Rob|author2=Stokkermans, Karel|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/europa-poy.html |title=European Footballer of the Year ("Ballon d'Or") |publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] |date=2009-12-11 |access-date=2010-05-26}}</ref>
*<small>FIFA</small>. {{note label|fifa||a}}{{note label|fifa||b}}{{note label|fifa||c}}{{note label|fifa||d}}{{note label|fifa||e}}{{note label|fifa||f}}{{note label|fifa||g}} Won the [[FIFA World Player of the Year]]/[[The Best FIFA Men's Player]] award while at Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/awards/playeroftheyear/winnermen.html |title=FIFA World Player |publisher=[[FIFA|Fédération Internationale de Football Association]] (FIFA) |access-date=2010-05-26 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100528002627/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/awards/playeroftheyear/winnermen.html |archive-date=2010-05-28 }}</ref>

*<small>Pichichi</small>.{{note label|Pichichi||a}}{{note label|Pichichi||b}}{{note label|Pichichi||c}}{{note label|Pichichi||d}}{{note label|Pichichi||e}}{{note label|Pichichi||f}}{{note label|Pichichi||g}}{{note label|Pichichi||h}}{{note label|Pichichi||i}}{{note label|Pichichi||j}}{{note label|Pichichi||k}}{{note label|Pichichi||l}}{{note label|Pichichi||m}}{{note label|Pichichi||n}}{{note label|Pichichi||o}}{{note label|Pichichi||p}} Won the [[Pichichi Trophy]] while at Real Madrid.<ref name=spantops>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spantops.html |title=Spain – List of Topscorers ("Pichichi") |publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] (RSSSF) |access-date=2010-04-09 |date=2009-06-12 |first=Luis Javier |last=Bravo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304084634/http://www.rsssf.com/tabless/spantops.html |archive-date=2016-03-04 }}</ref>

; Records and statistics
*A. {{note|Arthur}} [[Arthur Johnson (footballer, born 1879)|Arthur Johnson]] was the first player to score a goal in an official match in Real Madrid's history.
*B. {{note|Lazcano}} [[Jaime Lazcano]] was the first player to score a goal in [[La Liga]] in Real Madrid's history.
*C. {{note|Zamora and Vicente}} [[Ricardo Zamora]] and [[José Vicente Train]] both holds Real's record of [[Zamora Trophy|Zamora trophies]], with three won each.
*D. {{note|Chus}} [[Chus Alonso]] was the first Real Madrid player to score in an official match at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]].
*E. {{note|Di Stefano}} [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] was the first Real Madrid player to win the [[Ballon d'Or]] in 1957.
*F. {{note|Puskas}} [[Ferenc Puskás|Puskás]] is the record goalscorer in one match, with six goals.
*G. {{note|Santillana and Puskas}} Puskás and [[Santillana (footballer)|Santillana]] are Real's record goalscorers in the Spanish Cup, with 49 each.
*H. {{note|Santillana}} Santillana is Real's record goalscorer in the Spanish League Cup, with 8.
*I. {{note|Hugo}} [[Hugo Sánchez]] was the first Real Madrid player to win the [[European Golden Shoe]] in 1990.
*J. {{note|Zamorano}} [[Iván Zamorano]] scored the fastest goal in Real's history, 13 seconds after the start of the game.
*K. {{note|Míchel}} [[Míchel (footballer, born 1963)|Míchel]] is Real Madrid's record most assists in all competitions.
*L. {{note|Raul}} [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] is the club's record appearance maker in all competitions and in [[La Liga]] (with 550).
*M. {{note|Figo}} [[Luís Figo]] was the first Real Madrid player to win the [[FIFA World Player of the Year]] award, in 2001.
*N. {{note|Ramos}} [[Sergio Ramos]] has made the most international appearances as Real Madrid player, with 176 games played.
*O. {{note|Modrić}} [[Luka Modrić]] hold the record for the most trophies won at the club (28).
*P. {{note|Cristiano}} [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] is Real Madrid's record goalscorer in all competitions, record goalscorer in [[La Liga]] (with 311), record goalscorer in Europe (with 107), including a record 105 goals in the UEFA Champions league, the club's record league scorer in a single season, with 48 goals, and record scorer in all competitions in one season, with 61 goals, player with the highest number of European Golden Shoes (3), player with the highest number of hat-tricks in Spain (36), including a record 34 in La Liga, first player to score five goals twice in La Liga games, player with the highest number of goals in a single UEFA Champions League season, with 17, first player to score against all of the opposition teams in La Liga in a single season and first player to win three or more Ballon d'Or (in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017).
*Q. {{note|Benzema}} [[Karim Benzema]] holds the record of appearances for Real Madrid as a foreign player.
*R. {{note|Diomande}} [[Yan Diomande]] is the club's record signing, with a base transfer fee of €125 million, potentially rising to €140 million through add-ons.
